text:
Maya (CS): heads up — AcmeAnalytics reporting spike of 503s on hosted inference since ~02:00 UTC, their nightly ingestion is failing, they opened a ticket INC-4921. stacktrace attached by customer shows upstream worker crash.

Sam (oncall): pinging eng-runtime and infra. Can you share sample request ids?

Maya (CS): sent 3 request ids in the ticket: req_8f4a, req_8f4b, req_8f50. Customer says errors are intermittent but started after deployment last night. Severity P1 for them.

InfraBot: deploy event: cluster/us-west-gpu-pool scaled to 18 -> 24 nodes at 2026-03-15T01:57:12Z (autoscaler).

Alice P: looking at logs for those request ids now. Early signal: worker process exited with SIGSEGV and container restarted repeatedly.

Ben L: I see a pattern — several containers hit OOM shortly before segfault. Maybe memory fragmentation + cuda alloc failure. Extract from node logs:

```
Mar 15 02:04:08 gpu-worker-12 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 32145 (inference) score 1000 or sacrifice child
Mar 15 02:04:08 gpu-worker-12 inference[32145]: runtime error: CUDA out of memory when allocating 1.2GiB
Mar 15 02:04:09 gpu-worker-12 inference[32145]: fatal signal 11 (SIGSEGV) at 0x0000000000000000
Mar 15 02:04:09 gpu-worker-12 systemd: Started container restart.
```

Sasha R: interesting — OOM then segfault. Could be our allocator returning a null pointer then hitting a deref. Which model type are these requests hitting?

Maya (CS): customer says they're on rdlx-3.7-large-quant (quantized variant).

Ben L: quantized model + recent driver change could make memory handling more fragile. Any recent infra changes?

Sam (oncall): DeployBot shows kernel/driver rollout completed at 2026-03-15T01:45UTC to nvidia-driver 525.85 -> 530.11 on us-west nodes.

DeployBot: rollout/driver-upgrade/us-west completed (24 nodes) by infra-ops.

Alice P: correlating timestamps: driver upgrade finished ~10m before spike. Multiple nodes show post-upgrade OOMs.

Sasha R: repro plan — try replaying a batch of their request shape against rdlx-3.7-large-quant on a node with 530.11 driver. If we reproduce OOM + segv, try same on a 525.85 node.

Ben L: quick mitigation for hosted: add a soft cap on max_batch_tokens for that model route and enable fallback to rdlx-3.7-large (non-quant) until fixed. I'll push a canary config.

Sam (oncall): can we throttle their concurrent requests immediately? Customer wants a hotfix.

Maya (CS): AcmeAnalytics asked for a mitigation that avoids restarts — they prefer transient throttling to keep pipeline alive.

Ben L: rolling a config change to reduce route concurrency and set max_batch_tokens=4096 for rdlx-3.7-large-quant. Patch id: CFG-7812.

InfraBot: config change CFG-7812 applied to route rdlx-3.7-large-quant (canary 10% -> 100%) at 2026-03-15T02:10Z.

Alice P: ran repro locally on node with 530.11 — reproduced CUDA OOM on batch size 8 with payload shape the customer uses. On 525.85 the same sequence did not OOM. Logs show different allocation path lengths.

Sasha R: that strongly suggests driver ABI interaction with our quantized allocator. Next steps: 1) pin quantized model routes to older driver while drivers are rolled back or 2) request infra to pause driver rollout and investigate.

Sam (oncall): infra-ops, can we pause the rest of the driver rollout and consider rolling back?

Customer Success - Raj: Acme on call now, they confirm throttling reduced failures. They still want ETA for full fix.

InfraBot: rollback plan template: rollback-driver -> drain nodes -> reimage -> verify. Approving requires infra-ops engagement.

Ben L: I'm working on a temporary guard in the runtime allocator to refuse allocations above threshold and return a graceful 429 instead of OOM/segv. If we ship CFG-7813 it'll limit the runtime crash surface.

Sam (oncall): tagging this incident INC-4921. Action owners: Ben (mitigation code + route guard), Sasha (repro + driver diff), Alice (logs + customer comm), infra-ops (driver rollback).

Alice P: putting suggested customer communication in ticket: "We identified a correlation between a recent NVIDIA driver upgrade and upstream worker OOMs affecting quantized models. We have applied throttling to your route as a temporary measure. Our engineering team is investigating and will follow up with timeline."

Maya (CS): customer acknowledged, appreciates throttling.

Ben L: pushed runtime guard branch and canary CFG-7813 -> rolled to canary group at 02:40. Observing telemetry now.

DeployBot: config update CFG-7813 applied to canary nodes (10%).

Alice P: telemetry after throttling + guard: error rate for Acme dropped from 18% 503 -> 1.2% 429/blocked. No new segfaults observed in the last 15m.

Sam (oncall): good temporary win. Sasha — can you get a kernel/driver regression test added to our preflight matrix for quantized models?

Sasha R: will add a nightly job that runs quantized model binary against multiple drivers and records alloc traces. Filed issue INF-2047.

InfraBot: infra-ops acknowledged: pausing further driver rollouts in us-west. Engineer assigned: @chloe_ops.

chloe_ops: investigating rollback scope and ETA. Likely 2-4 hours to roll back and validate.

Maya (CS): Acme asked for an ETA; told them 3-4 hours and we asked for patience.

Sam (oncall): summary for the incident channel: root cause suspected driver/allocator interaction causing CUDA OOM leading to segfaults in quantized runtime. Mitigation: throttling + runtime allocation guard + driver rollout paused. Owners listed.

Maya (CS): closing the thread for now — will update with postmortem once infra and eng confirm rollback status. :thumbsup:
